source_caption:
Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man — Friendship, Loyalty & Revenge
Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man (1991) follows two longtime friends, Harley Davidson and Marlboro, two rebellious outlaws who return to Los Angeles and discover that their old friend’s bar is about to be taken away by a powerful financial corporation.
Determined to help, the two friends decide to rob a money shipment to save the bar. But their plan goes completely wrong when they accidentally steal a dangerous package belonging to a ruthless criminal organization.
Now hunted by heavily armed enemies, Harley and Marlboro must rely on their courage, loyalty, and street skills to survive. What started as a simple attempt to help a friend quickly turns into a deadly fight against people far more powerful than they expected.
The film explores themes of friendship, loyalty, freedom, revenge, and standing up against powerful forces. At its heart, the story is about two friends who refuse to abandon each other, even when the odds are completely against them.
What makes Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man compelling is the chemistry between its two rebellious leads and their willingness to risk everything for friendship.
💬 They weren't looking for trouble—but when trouble came, they faced it together.

source_details.synopsis: Harley Davidson and the Marlboro Man is a 1991 American neo-Western biker buddy action film directed by Simon Wincer and starring Mickey Rourke, Don Johnson, Chelsea Field, Tom Sizemore, Vanessa Williams (who also contributes to the film's soundtrack), Daniel Baldwin, Giancarlo Esposito and Robert Ginty. Set in the near future United States, it concerns two friends–a melancholic biker and a world-weary bullrider–who rob the bank threatening their favorite bar with foreclosure in hopes of paying it off with its own money, only to discover that it is a front for a criminal cartel.
